advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Align the placeholders in the AGENTS.md worktree example so the path leaf and branch use the same token (e.g. `.rebar/worktrees/<branch> -b <branch>`).
evidence: AGENTS.md:441: `(git fetch origin && git worktree add .rebar/worktrees/<name> -b <branch> origin/main; or`

The Makefile recipe uses a single `$(name)` for both path leaf and branch: Makefile:240 `target_dir="$(if $(dir),$(dir),.rebar/worktrees/$(name))"` and Makefile:246 `git worktree add "$$target_dir" -b "$(name)"`
advisory.finding: The touched AGENTS.md worktree example mixes placeholder names: `git worktree add .rebar/worktrees/<name> -b <branch> origin/main` uses `<name>` for the path but `<branch>` for the branch, so a reader copying it substitutes two different tokens for what is a single value (the Makefile's `name=` becomes both the path leaf and the branch). This mismatch predates the diff but sits on the modified line.
scenarios: A reader copies the AGENTS.md snippet and picks inconsistent values for the directory leaf vs the branch name.
advisory.suggested_fix: Change the AGENTS.md example to `git worktree add .rebar/worktrees/<branch> -b <branch> origin/main`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Drop the verbatim `target_dir=...` source-text assertion in test_worktree_recipe_does_not_feed_make_comments_to_shell; the default-path behavior is already covered by the real-recipe execution in test_default_worktree_path_stays_inside_repo_sandbox.
evidence: tests/unit/test_makefile_worktree.py:192-194: assert f"worktree add .rebar/worktrees/{BRANCH} -b {BRANCH} origin/main" in (tmp_path / "git-args.txt").read_text(...) — the same default-path behavior is already verified through the real executed recipe

Litmus (Rule 4): the exact-string assertion would break if the recipe line were reformatted or the shell variable renamed, with no observable-behavior change — a change-detector, not a behavior-verifier.
advisory.finding: test_worktree_recipe_does_not_feed_make_comments_to_shell asserts on the verbatim TEXT of the Makefile recipe (the executable unit under test, which test 1 actually runs) rather than its observable behavior. The assertion `assert '\ttarget_dir="$(if $(dir),$(dir),.rebar/worktrees/$(name))"; \\' in recipe_lines` is an exact source-text match that breaks on any behavior-preserving change (reformatting, whitespace, renaming target_dir, splitting the line) with no change in observable behavior. It is a source-grepping change-detector, and the behavior it purports to verify (the default worktree path) is already covered behaviorally by test_default_worktree_path_stays_inside_repo_sandbox, which drives the real recipe and asserts the emitted 'worktree add .rebar/worktrees/<branch>' git args.
advisory.suggested_fix: Remove the exact-string `in recipe_lines` assertion (line 220). If the intent is to guard the make-comment-in-continued-line parse hazard, keep only the behavioral guard already present in test 1 (`assert "/bin/sh: branch:" not in combined`), which detects the same defect via observable output regardless of recipe text layout.
